title: RuleAddSpec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> rule add <spec.json>` — the rule to persist. The rule is validated against the real kernel before writing, and the persisted model is re-validated (so every declared message locale must be covered).

field.description: the error field's ABSOLUTE path, e.g. /Order/Quantity; its parent group becomes the rule group (iteration scope) UNLESS `group` overrides it. PLACEMENT LAW: a rule iterates over every repeatable group whose per-row fields it references, and the error field MUST lie inside each of those groups (else MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP where it lies outside the rule group, and MVK_NO_WILDCARD — or MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NO_INDEX for a parallel index-keyed group — where it lies inside). So for a per-row rule ('each row must …') pick an error field INSIDE the repeatable group; for a whole-document rule aggregate the per-row operands, starring EVERY repeatable level the path crosses (e.g. Sum(Group*/Field), Sum(Outer*/Inner*/Field)), and use a non-repeatable error field — a level left unstarred still reads per row. Tip: choose the error field at the lowest group that contains all referenced fields — relative paths stay short and survive a group move.

group.description: OPTIONAL rule group / iteration scope — an ABSOLUTE group path; defaults to the error field's parent. Override it for an operator whose rule must sit at the PARENT of a repeated group with the error field INSIDE it: `RepetitionNotUnique` needs `group:/Order` with `field:/Order/Items/Sku`. It is the same iteration scope `rule check` validates against (its group option), so a checked rule persists unchanged. This verb requires the error field to lie inside the group, which is STRICTER THAN THE KERNEL and a deliberate narrowing rather than a kernel law: the kernel imposes containment only once the rule ITERATES — it reads a per-row field of a repeatable group — and then demands the error field be inside THAT group (MVK_ERROR_FIELD_NOT_IN_RULEGROUP), exactly as it does for a computation's computed field.

condition.description: the condition in A12 DSL — TRUE on a VIOLATION/the error scenario (the rule fires when it holds), so to enforce a requirement write its violation, e.g. FieldNotFilled(X) not FieldFilled(X)

comment.description: optional explanatory note, persisted as a leading ;; comment on the rule's condition

allowDifferingDecimals.description: the editor's 'Allow Differing Decimal Places' — prepend @SuppressWarning(MVK_INVALID_COMPARE_DEC_PLACES) so an otherwise-incompatible numeric == / != derived-scale/capability pair is accepted (the kernel's one suppressible warning). Default false.

annotation.description: OPTIONAL name→value annotations to set on the rule at add time (a rule has no label slot; change them later with `dmtool meta <ref>`). Read back via `rule read` under `annotations`.

internal-description.description: OPTIONAL per-locale (locale→text) internal description on the rule; read back via `rule read` under `internalDescription`.

external-description.description: OPTIONAL per-locale (locale→text) external description on the rule; read back via `rule read` under `externalDescription`.

messages.description: ≥1 localized message; cover every locale the model declares

locale.description: a full locale code, e.g. en_US (bare 'en' is rejected by the kernel)

text.description: the message text; may interpolate kernel tokens, each using a model path: $<Field>.value$ (the field's runtime value), $<Field>$ (its localized label), $#<Group>$ (a repeatable group's 1-based row index). The group token takes an ABSOLUTE path and the named group must CONTAIN this rule — its own group or any ancestor; RuleGroup and RootGroup are shorthands for the two ends of that chain, a group elsewhere is INVALID_GROUP, and a first segment naming no declared root is INVALID_ROOT_GROUP. A LITERAL dollar sign is written $$.

examples.comment: cap the monthly fee per policy
